city_center.notes: the Flatirons are visible from nearly every street corner and define Boulder's western skyline; the Boulder County Farmers Market (13th Street) brings Western Slope fruit and Front Range produce to town Wed + Sat. sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Flatirons; gocolorado.com/boulder; bcfm.org.

cultural_notes: the Flatirons are five massive tilted slabs of Fountain Formation conglomeratic sandstone (roughly 290-296 million years old), rising directly above the western edge of town and visible from nearly every street corner (source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Flatirons; gocolorado.com/boulder)
Boulder is a trail-and-outdoor town: 155+ miles of trails and an open-space greenbelt wrap the city, feeding a health-forward, active-lifestyle food culture (source: gocolorado.com/boulder)

the Boulder County Farmers Market (13th Street, Sat Apr-Nov) is a Front Range destination for Western Slope peaches from Palisade and Paonia and organic local produce (source: bcfm.org markets; bcfm.org Western Slope farmers)
the Flatirons and Chautauqua are the civic-recreation heart -- morning-trail-then-breakfast rhythm is the local ritual (INFERRED civic framing from region knowledge -- verify tone before production)
